before.title: 2.5 GDI engine stalls while stopped in Drive — ECU neutral-control software defect (Grandeur GN7)
before.description: Shortly after the GN7 launched, Hyundai opened a free-repair campaign for 4,818 Grandeur 2.5 GDI cars built November 16, 2022 - January 2, 2023 because the engine could stall while the car sat in Drive with the brake applied. During prolonged stops the transmission's 'neutral control' releases hydraulic pressure to save fuel; the ECU software handled electrical loads in this state poorly, causing unstable idle RPM followed by the engine shutting off. Korean outlets (Motorgraph, M Today/AutoDaily) covered the campaign, which was one of roughly 20 free-repair/recall actions logged against the GN7 in its first year.
before.solution: Apply Hyundai's free ECU software update — delivered over-the-air via Bluelink for connected cars, or in about 20 minutes at a Hyundai direct service center or Blue Hands branch for others. No hardware replacement is required. Any GN7 2.5 GDI from the affected production window that exhibits unstable idle or stalling at a stop should have the campaign status checked at car.go.kr or a dealer.
symptoms: Unstable or fluctuating idle RPM while stopped in Drive with the brake pressed
Engine shuts off on its own during a prolonged stop
Restart required at traffic lights
Possible warning lights after the stall

before.title: C-MDPS steering column clunk and rattle (Grandeur IG)
before.description: Grandeur IG models (including the 2020+ facelift) with column-mounted electric power steering (C-MDPS) commonly develop a rattling, knocking or 'clunking' noise when the wheel is turned at a stop or at low speed. The noise comes from wear in the steering column's damping components — the flexible coupling and column bearing that prevent metal-to-metal contact. As the parts wear, owners also report increased steering play and a vague or notchy steering feel. The complaint is heavily documented across Korean owner communities (Bobaedream, Clien, AutoView boards) and on Namu Wiki's 6th-generation Grandeur page. Hyundai never declared it an official defect, but Blue Hands service centers perform goodwill free repairs — originally just the coupling/bearing, and more recently full MDPS assembly replacement when needed.
before.solution: Take the car to a Hyundai Blue Hands or direct service center and reproduce the noise; Hyundai has been replacing the worn coupling/bearing — and in persistent cases the entire MDPS assembly — free of charge as a goodwill repair even out of warranty. If paying out of pocket at an independent shop, a coupling replacement is cheap, while a full column/MDPS unit replacement is a four-figure job in USD terms.
symptoms: Rattle or knock from the steering column when turning at a standstill or low speed
Clicking/grinding felt through the steering wheel rim
Increased free play in the steering wheel
Vague or notchy steering feel as wear progresses

before.title: Engine front case (timing cover) oil leak (Grandeur IG)
before.description: A chronic problem (고질병) repeatedly cited in Korean owner communities for the Grandeur IG — and its Kia K7 sibling — is engine oil seepage from the front case (timing chain cover), typically appearing after roughly 50,000 km. The sealant between the front case and the block degrades, letting oil weep down the front of the engine; documented cases on the 3.0 V6 describe undercarriage panels soaked in oil, and the issue is also widely reported on 2.4 GDI cars. CV-joint (등속조인트) grease/oil leaks are mentioned alongside it as a related underbody finding during used-car inspections. Left alone, the leak worsens, can foul the drive belt area and triggers low-oil-level conditions.
before.solution: Confirm the source with a degrease-and-recheck or UV dye test, since valve cover and CV-joint leaks look similar. The fix is to remove the front timing cover, clean both surfaces, and reseal with fresh liquid gasket — a labor-intensive job (roughly 300,000-700,000 KRW at Korean shops, a few hundred USD). Cars still inside the powertrain warranty have had it resealed free at Hyundai service centers; used-car performance-guarantee insurance has also covered it. Check the oil level regularly until repaired.
symptoms: Oil seepage or wet residue on the front of the engine block
Oil spots under the front of the car
Burning oil smell after driving
Engine oil level slowly dropping between services
Oil-soaked underbody covers found during inspection

before.title: Hybrid electronic brake software lets car roll back on hills — official MOLIT recall (Grandeur GN7 HEV)
before.description: In April 2023 Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport announced an official recall of 14,316 Grandeur GN7 hybrids for a configuration error in the electronic (integrated) brake system software. When Smart Cruise Control brought the car to a stop behind another vehicle on an uphill grade, the brake system could release insufficiently and let the car roll backward, creating a collision risk with vehicles behind. This was one of two official GN7 recalls in spring 2023 — alongside roughly 20 free-repair campaigns — that drew heavy Korean press criticism of the model's launch quality.
before.solution: Have the free electronic-brake software update performed; the recall campaign started May 2, 2023 at Hyundai Hi-Tech Centers and Blue Hands branches. MOLIT notes that owners who previously paid to repair this defect can claim reimbursement from Hyundai. Owners can check VIN-specific applicability on the official Korean recall site (car.go.kr).
symptoms: Car rolls backward after Smart Cruise Control stops it on an uphill slope
Insufficient brake holding force at a standstill on grades
Driver must press the brake pedal to prevent rollback

before.title: Launch-year electrical faults: door-handle touch sensors, LED driver modules, hybrid battery drain, parking-sensor communication (Grandeur GN7)
before.description: First-year GN7s (production roughly October 2022 - February 2023) accumulated a cluster of documented electrical defects, each with its own Hyundai free-repair or recall campaign: (1) door-handle touch sensors with faulty internal logic that fail to unlock the flush door handles (8,475 cars); (2) LED driver modules (LDM) that intermittently cut headlamp/DRL output in cold weather (1,961 cars); (3) hybrid battery management system software errors causing intermittent 12V battery discharge and no-start mornings (6,006 cars, fixed via OTA); (4) power trunk/tailgate control firmware faults (1,524 cars); and (5) an official March 2023 recall of about 11,200 vehicles for communication failure between the vehicle controller and parking sensors, disabling the rear parking-distance warning and raising back-over collision risk. Korean press tallied about 20 such actions in the model's first year, affecting over 300,000 cumulative repair targets.
before.solution: All items are covered by Hyundai free-repair campaigns or the MOLIT recall: software/firmware updates for the door-handle sensors, BMS, power tailgate, and parking-sensor communication (many deliverable over-the-air via Bluelink), and physical replacement of affected LED driver modules. Check the VIN at car.go.kr or a Hyundai service center to confirm which campaigns apply; owners who paid for these repairs can seek reimbursement.
symptoms: Flush door handles fail to respond to touch and won't unlock the car
LED headlights or daytime running lights flicker or go out in cold weather
Dead 12V battery / no-start after parking overnight (hybrid)
Power trunk or tailgate fails to open or close properly
Rear parking-distance warning silent or erratic when reversing

before.title: Theta II 2.4 GDI connecting-rod bearing wear and engine seizure (Grandeur IG 2.4)
before.description: The 2.4L Theta II GDI engine offered in the pre-facelift Grandeur IG (2017-2019, before the 2.5 Smartstream replaced it) is part of the Theta II family covered by Hyundai's Korea-market recall and lifetime engine warranty. Machining debris and oil-supply problems cause connecting-rod bearing wear that progresses to rod knock, cylinder-wall scuffing, heavy oil consumption and, in the worst cases, sudden engine seizure while driving. MOLIT-supervised recalls installed the KSDS knock-sensor detection software, which puts the car in reduced-power limp mode (often with code P1326) when bearing noise is detected, and Hyundai extended a lifetime warranty on the engine for Grandeur HG/IG among roughly 520,000 Korean vehicles (4.69 million worldwide). Korean owner communities (Bobaedream, Clien) consistently report oil-consumption and knock cases on IG 2.4 cars.
before.solution: Have the KSDS software recall performed and, at any sign of knock, oil consumption or a P1326 code, present the car to a Hyundai service center for the Theta II bearing inspection. Engines that fail inspection are replaced with a new short/long block free of charge under the lifetime Theta II warranty (Korea and US); Hyundai also reimburses prior out-of-pocket repairs and towing. Outside warranty coverage, a replacement engine runs several thousand dollars. Use the correct oil and check the level frequently between services.
symptoms: Metallic knocking or rod-knock noise from the engine, especially at cold start
Engine oil level drops noticeably between oil changes
Check-engine light with P1326 and reduced-power limp mode
Loss of power or hesitation under acceleration
Sudden engine stall or seizure while driving in severe cases

proposal.title: Theta II 2.4 GDI Connecting-Rod Bearing Coverage and KSDS (Grandeur IG)
proposal.description: Hyundai identifies the Grandeur among Korea-market Theta II GDI vehicles receiving expanded Knock Sensor Detection System (KSDS) coverage and a lifetime engine warranty limited to connecting-rod-bearing seizure. Hyundai's official 2019 Grandeur specification identifies its engine as the improved Theta II 2.4 GDi. Hyundai's disclosure also provides compensation terms for eligible customers who experienced engine stoppage or fire because of the covered engine defect.
proposal.solution: Ask a Hyundai service center to check the VIN for applicable KSDS and engine-warranty coverage. KSDS is monitoring software rather than a mechanical repair; any inspection, warranty decision or engine repair depends on the vehicle's eligibility and Hyundai's diagnosis.
symptoms: Engine stoppage in a covered connecting-rod-bearing-seizure case
Engine fire in a covered engine-defect case
